name: WILLCOX, Andrew

headline.note: First-person and party profiles establish a long career in the Willcox family tomato-farming enterprise, including ownership and management before a structured family sale in 2010. Official council records establish local elected office from 2012 to 15 June 2022. The farming commencement, entity history, workload and leave are not sufficiently documented, and local and federal elected office are excluded. No public/private full-time headline total is calculable.

career_spells.evidence_note: Willcox and party profiles describe him as a third-generation tomato farmer who worked in the family farm, later purchased and managed it, expanded domestic and export supply, and operated it with his wife, sister and brother-in-law. A detailed 2017 profile says Willcox and his wife sold their interest to the other family operators in 2010. The commencement, employing entities, ownership transitions, hours and leave are not fully published; the statement that he purchased the business at age 27 is not converted into an invented calendar date.
career_spells.counting_note: Substantive private farming activity is supported, but the unresolved boundaries, entities and workload prevent a documented full-time duration.

career_spells.employer: Private investments and small businesses, entities not identified
career_spells.evidence_note: Current political profiles call Willcox a small-business owner, while the 2017 career profile refers to off-farm investments that he and his wife managed alongside the farm. The entities, activities, dates, remuneration and workload are not identified, including whether these continued during elected office.
career_spells.counting_note: The evidence is too general to define or count an employment spell.

career_spells.evidence_note: Whitsunday Regional Council's 2021-22 annual report says Willcox was first elected in 2012 as Division 6 councillor and was sworn in as mayor on 4 April 2016. The exact 2012 commencement day is not stated in the sources reviewed.

Council records give swearing-in on 4 April 2016, unopposed re-election in April 2020 and resignation on 15 June 2022 after the federal poll was declared. Council minutes also record leave during the 2022 federal campaign.
Contemporary reporting records LNP endorsement on 29 August 2021. Council material records campaign leave in April 2022. No separate paid party employment is established.
career_spells.counting_note: Candidate and party activity is excluded.

career_spells.role: Member of the House of Representatives for Dawson
career_spells.evidence_note: The Parliamentary Handbook records election for Dawson on 21 May 2022 and re-election in 2025.
